notes: Mood set redesigned to reflect documented Christian faith-journey experiences (LifeWay Research on doubt, Barna Group research on spiritual transformation stages, Ignatian consolation/desolation, and the extensively documented phenomenon of spiritual dryness) rather than generic secular mood vocabulary.

verses.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God. My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
